<content class="appendix">
    <para id="import-auto-id2205639">This table lists selected emissions. Decay modes are alpha decay (α), beta-minus decay (β−), positron emission (β+), electron capture (EC), and isomeric transition (IT). The suffix m identifies a metastable nuclear state. Alpha energies are the kinetic energies of the emitted particles, excluding daughter-nucleus recoil. Beta energies are spectrum endpoints; the mean energy depends on the spectrum and is not generally half the endpoint. EC and IT have no particle energy listed in that column.</para>
<para id="appendix-b-yield-conventions">Particle yields are emitted particles per 100 decays of the listed isotope; entries beside EC or IT give decays through that mode per 100 decays. Photon yields are gamma photons per 100 parent decays, including the indicated daughter de-excitations, rather than probabilities for transitions that can also produce conversion electrons. Daughter isomers can delay photon emission. The left and right entries on the same line are independent lists, not necessarily coincident emissions. Only selected emissions are shown; yields need not sum to 100. X-rays, conversion electrons, annihilation photons, and later radioactive-daughter emissions are omitted, except for the listed Ba-137m and Mn-52m transitions following Cs-137 and Fe-52 decay.</para>
